en: village; hamlet; historic quarter outside the old walls
ex: Il borgo medievale si arrampica sul colle con le sue case di pietra e i tetti di coppi.
exEn: The medieval village climbs the hill with its stone houses and terracotta roofs.
note: Historically the built-up area just outside the city walls; today evokes small, picturesque old towns (i borghi più belli d'Italia). Diminutive: borghetto.

en: district (of a town, esp. Siena); country lane (regional)
ex: A Siena ogni contrada ha il proprio stemma, la propria chiesa e una rivalità secolare con le vicine.
exEn: In Siena every contrada has its own coat of arms, its own church and a centuries-old rivalry with its neighbours.
note: Best known for the seventeen contrade that compete in the Palio di Siena. In northern dialects and older usage also 'street, lane'.

en: district of Venice (one of six); sestiere
ex: Il sestiere di Cannaregio conserva ancora un'atmosfera schiettamente popolare.
exEn: The Cannaregio sestiere still retains a genuinely working-class atmosphere.
note: From 'sesto' (a sixth). Used also of Genoa and Rapallo; the Venetian ones are Cannaregio, Castello, Dorsoduro, San Marco, San Polo, Santa Croce.

en: arcaded gallery; loggia running along a façade
ex: Dal loggiato del primo piano si dominava l'intera piazza del mercato.
exEn: From the first-floor loggia one overlooked the whole market square.
note: Architectural term; a 'loggia' is a single open gallery, a 'loggiato' a continuous series of arches on columns.

ex: I bastioni cinquecenteschi di Lucca sono diventati una passeggiata alberata amatissima dai cittadini.
exEn: Lucca's sixteenth-century ramparts have become a tree-lined promenade much loved by the townspeople.
note: Military architecture; plural often refers to the whole ring of walls (i bastioni di Milano). Figurative: 'bastione della tradizione'.

en: city walls; ring of fortified walls
ex: La cinta muraria aureliana si snoda per quasi diciannove chilometri attorno alla Roma antica.
exEn: The Aurelian walls wind for almost nineteen kilometres around ancient Rome.
note: Fixed technical expression (also 'cerchia muraria'). 'Cinta' alone means enclosure, girdle.

ex: Un viottolo lastricato scendeva ripido tra gli orti fino alla chiesa.
exEn: A paved footpath ran steeply down between the vegetable gardens to the church.
note: Diminutive of 'via' with a slightly rustic flavour; also 'viottola' (f). Cf. 'sentiero' (path in nature), 'vicolo' (urban alley).

en: narrow street or alley in Venice
ex: Ci perdemmo in un dedalo di calli che finivano tutte sull'acqua.
exEn: We got lost in a maze of alleys that all ended at the water.
note: Venetian term (from Latin callis). Related Venetian words: 'campo' (square), 'rio' (canal), 'fondamenta' (quay street), 'salizada' (paved street).

ex: Nel campiello dietro la chiesa i bambini giocavano tra i panni stesi.
exEn: In the little square behind the church children were playing among the hanging washing.
note: Venetian diminutive of 'campo', the Venetian word for a square; only Piazza San Marco is called 'piazza'.

en: great tower; keep of a castle
ex: Il torrione angolare della rocca fu rinforzato per resistere alle nuove artiglierie.
exEn: The corner tower of the fortress was reinforced to withstand the new artillery.
note: Augmentative of 'torre'; refers specifically to a massive round or square defensive tower. Cf. 'mastio' (keep, donjon).

ex: La merlatura guelfa, a merli quadrati, distingue il palazzo comunale da quello ghibellino a coda di rondine.
exEn: The Guelph crenellation, with square merlons, distinguishes the town hall from the Ghibelline swallow-tailed kind.
note: From 'merlo' (merlon). Guelph battlements are square, Ghibelline ones are 'a coda di rondine' (swallow-tailed).

ex: Le ruote della carrozza sobbalzavano sul selciato sconnesso della via.
exEn: The carriage wheels jolted over the uneven cobbles of the street.
note: From 'selce' (flint). Cf. 'lastricato' (flagstone paving), 'acciottolato' (pebble paving), 'sampietrini' (Roman cobbles).

ex: L'acciottolato del cortile, di ciottoli di fiume, era scivoloso dopo la pioggia.
exEn: The courtyard's pebble paving, made of river stones, was slippery after the rain.
note: From 'ciottolo' (pebble); paving made of rounded stones set in sand, typical of old courtyards and Ligurian 'risseu' mosaics.

ex: Le nobildonne veneziane si schiarivano i capelli al sole sull'altana.
exEn: Venetian noblewomen used to lighten their hair in the sun on the rooftop terrace.
note: A wooden platform built above the roof, characteristic of Venice; also a raised loggia on Roman and Tuscan palaces.

en: arcade; colonnade; portico running along a street
ex: Sotto il porticato che costeggia la piazza si riparano dal sole i venditori ambulanti.
exEn: Under the arcade that runs along the square the street vendors shelter from the sun.
note: Collective of 'portico'; Bologna's famous arcades are 'i portici'. Also adjective: 'via porticata'.

ex: La facciata è scandita da lesene che ne alleggeriscono la massa.
exEn: The façade is articulated by pilaster strips that lighten its mass.
note: Specialist term of art history; unlike a 'pilastro' it has no structural function. Common in descriptions of Romanesque and Renaissance façades.

ex: Trastevere è il rione più pittoresco e ormai più turistico di Roma.
exEn: Trastevere is Rome's most picturesque and by now most touristy district.
note: From Latin regio; Rome's historic centre has 22 rioni. Elsewhere (Naples, Bologna) a popular neighbourhood; 'rionale' = of the neighbourhood (mercato rionale).

ex: Nei Promessi sposi Manzoni descrive il lazzaretto di Milano stipato di appestati.
exEn: In The Betrothed Manzoni describes the Milan lazaretto crammed with plague victims.
note: From the Venetian island of Santa Maria di Nazareth (first quarantine station, 1423). Figurative: a place full of the sick.

ex: Le università furono a lungo un baluardo di libertà contro l'oscurantismo.
exEn: Universities were long a bulwark of freedom against obscurantism.
note: Literal sense (defensive rampart) is historical; today mostly figurative and elevated. Cf. 'roccaforte'.

ex: Al crocicchio dei due sentieri una madonnina di ceramica vegliava sui viandanti.
exEn: At the crossing of the two paths a little ceramic Madonna watched over travellers.
note: Literary and rustic; the neutral word is 'incrocio'. Related learned words: 'trivio', 'quadrivio'.

en: parvis; churchyard in front of a church
ex: Gli sposi uscirono sul sagrato sotto una pioggia di riso.
exEn: The newlyweds came out onto the parvis under a shower of rice.
note: From 'sacrato' (consecrated ground). The open space in front of a church, often raised by a few steps.

ex: Le pievi romaniche della campagna toscana custodiscono fonti battesimali millenari.
exEn: The Romanesque parish churches of the Tuscan countryside preserve thousand-year-old baptismal fonts.
note: From Latin plebs. Frequent in place names (Pieve di Cadore, Pieve Santo Stefano); the priest of a pieve was the 'pievano'.

ex: Le guglie del Duomo di Milano si stagliano bianche contro il cielo di marzo.
exEn: The spires of Milan Cathedral stand out white against the March sky.
note: Also used for slender rock pinnacles in the Dolomites. The Madonnina stands on the 'guglia maggiore' of the Duomo.

en: huge ugly block of flats; barracks-like building
ex: Ai margini della città sorsero negli anni Sessanta casermoni grigi senza un albero attorno.
exEn: On the edge of the city, in the sixties, grey barracks-like blocks went up without a tree around them.
note: Pejorative augmentative of 'caserma'; colloquial-journalistic. Cf. 'palazzone', 'alveare' (fig.).

ex: La Darsena di Milano, un tempo porto fluviale, è oggi un luogo di ritrovo serale.
exEn: Milan's Darsena, once a river port, is today an evening meeting place.
note: From Arabic dar as-sina'a (the same root as 'arsenale'). A sheltered basin where boats moor or are repaired.

ex: Al lavatoio comunale le donne del paese si scambiavano notizie e pettegolezzi.
exEn: At the communal wash-house the village women exchanged news and gossip.
note: Historical civic structure, often covered, found in most old Italian villages; now mostly restored as heritage.

ex: Il giorno dei morti tutto il paese sale al camposanto con i crisantemi.
exEn: On All Souls' Day the whole village goes up to the cemetery with chrysanthemums.
note: More affective and old-fashioned than 'cimitero'; the Camposanto of Pisa is a monumental cemetery. Also written 'campo santo'.

ex: La baia offre un ancoraggio sicuro riparato dal maestrale.
exEn: The bay offers a safe anchorage sheltered from the mistral.
note: Nautical; also technical (fixing of a structure) and figurative ('un ancoraggio ai valori'). 'Diritti di ancoraggio' = anchorage dues.

ex: Con il vento contrario dovemmo procedere a lunghi bordeggi per rientrare in porto.
exEn: With a headwind we had to proceed in long tacks to get back to harbour.
note: From 'bordeggiare' (to tack). Each single leg is a 'bordo' ('andare di bolina' = to sail close-hauled).

ex: Le piccole navi da cabotaggio rifornivano un tempo tutti i porti della costa.
exEn: Small coasting vessels once supplied every port along the coast.
note: Technical maritime and legal term; 'piccolo/grande cabotaggio'. Figurative 'di piccolo cabotaggio' = small-scale, of limited ambition (un politico di piccolo cabotaggio).

ex: La prima circumnavigazione del globo fu completata dai superstiti della spedizione di Magellano.
exEn: The first circumnavigation of the globe was completed by the survivors of Magellan's expedition.
note: Learned Latinate compound; note the '-m-' (circum-), unlike 'circondare'. Verb: circumnavigare.

ex: Il beccheggio violento del traghetto fece star male metà dei passeggeri.
exEn: The ferry's violent pitching made half the passengers sick.
note: Bow-to-stern movement; contrasted with 'rollio' (side-to-side rolling). Verb: beccheggiare.

ex: Il lento rollio della nave ci cullava nelle cuccette.
exEn: The ship's slow rolling rocked us in our bunks.
note: Side-to-side motion; pair with 'beccheggio'. Verb: rollare. Note plural 'rollii' with double i.

ex: Il porto era considerato dai moralisti una sentina di ogni vizio.
exEn: The port was considered by moralists a sink of every vice.
note: Literal nautical sense (the lowest part of the hull where water collects) is rare; the figurative literary use is the one you will meet.

ex: Il vento fischiava tra il sartiame del veliero ormeggiato.
exEn: The wind whistled through the rigging of the moored sailing ship.
note: Collective noun from 'sartia' (shroud). Related: 'cordame', 'alberatura' (masts), 'velatura' (sails).

ex: Il nostromo fischiò l'adunata e l'equipaggio si radunò sul ponte.
exEn: The bosun whistled the muster and the crew gathered on deck.
note: From Catalan nostramo ('our master'). The petty officer in charge of the deck crew; frequent in sea fiction (Salgari, Conrad translations).

ex: Un viandante stanco bussò alla porta dell'osteria chiedendo un giaciglio.
exEn: A weary wayfarer knocked at the inn door asking for a place to sleep.
note: Literary and archaic; evokes fairy tales and nineteenth-century prose. Modern neutral term: 'viaggiatore'.

ex: Da giovane fece il musicista girovago per le piazze di mezza Europa.
exEn: As a young man he worked as an itinerant musician in the squares of half of Europe.
note: Used both as noun and adjective (compagnia girovaga). Slightly bohemian connotation; cf. 'vagabondo' (more negative), 'nomade'.

ex: La diligenza per Firenze partiva all'alba e impiegava due giorni.
exEn: The stagecoach for Florence left at dawn and took two days.
note: The travel sense is historical; the abstract sense ('con diligenza', 'la diligenza del buon padre di famiglia' in law) is current and formal.

ex: Una chiatta carica di ghiaia risaliva lentamente il Po.
exEn: A barge laden with gravel was slowly making its way up the Po.
note: Also 'ponte di chiatte' (pontoon bridge). Colloquial-jocular: a big flat clumsy shoe or foot.

en: ferryman; (fig.) person who steers a transition
ex: Il nuovo direttore fu scelto come traghettatore dell'azienda verso la fusione.
exEn: The new director was chosen to steer the company through the merger.
note: Literal sense recalls Caronte, 'il traghettatore delle anime'. Very common in political journalism: 'governo traghettatore'.

ex: Le navi da crociera restano alla fonda nella rada in attesa di un posto in banchina.
exEn: The cruise ships lie at anchor in the roadstead waiting for a berth.
note: Nautical; 'in rada', 'alla fonda' (at anchor). Do not confuse with 'rado' (sparse) or 'raid'.

ex: Il caccia scese in picchiata sul bersaglio e si rialzò all'ultimo istante.
exEn: The fighter dived on the target and pulled up at the last moment.
note: 'Scendere in picchiata'; figurative for prices, ratings: 'le azioni sono in picchiata'. Opposite: 'cabrata' (climb).

ex: Il pellegrino portava nella bisaccia un pane, un fiasco e il breviario.
exEn: The pilgrim carried in his knapsack a loaf, a flask and his breviary.
note: A double bag slung over the shoulder or a mule's back; rustic and literary. Plural keeps the 'c' without 'i': bisacce.

en: guest quarters; guesthouse (of a monastery, company or institution)
ex: L'abbazia ospita i visitatori nella foresteria, in cambio di un'offerta.
exEn: The abbey puts visitors up in its guesthouse in return for a donation.
note: From 'forestiero' (outsider, stranger). Now also company or university guest accommodation.

ex: La mostra itinerante toccherà dodici città prima di tornare a Roma.
exEn: The touring exhibition will visit twelve cities before returning to Rome.
note: Formal/journalistic; 'mostra itinerante', 'biblioteca itinerante', 'festival itinerante'. Cf. 'ambulante' (of street vendors).

en: of travel writing; relating to journeys (literature)
ex: La letteratura odeporica del Settecento riflette la moda del Grand Tour.
exEn: Eighteenth-century travel literature reflects the fashion for the Grand Tour.
note: Very learned (from Greek hodoiporikos); used almost only in 'letteratura/genere odeporico'. Noun: 'odeporica' (travel writing as a genre).

ex: Il torrente si è scavato una forra profonda tra pareti di roccia a picco.
exEn: The stream has carved itself a deep gorge between sheer rock walls.
note: Geographical/literary; cf. 'gola' (general), 'orrido' (dramatic gorge), 'canyon'. 'Torrentismo' = canyoning.

ex: Il profumo della macchia, di mirto e lentisco, arrivava fino alla spiaggia.
exEn: The scent of the maquis, of myrtle and mastic, reached all the way to the beach.
note: This botanical sense ('macchia mediterranea') is distinct from 'macchia' = stain/spot. 'Darsi alla macchia' = to go into hiding (from partisans hiding in the scrub).

en: gravelly riverbed; dry bed of a stream
ex: D'estate il fiume si riduce a un filo d'acqua in mezzo al greto bianco di sassi.
exEn: In summer the river shrinks to a trickle in the middle of its stone-white bed.
note: Refers to the stony, exposed part of a riverbed rather than the water; literary and geographical.

ex: I contrabbandieri nascondevano la merce negli anfratti della scogliera.
exEn: The smugglers hid their goods in the clefts of the cliff.
note: Literary; figurative 'gli anfratti dell'anima/della memoria' (hidden corners). Adj. 'anfrattuoso'.

ex: Un nevischio pungente sferzava i volti dei passanti.
exEn: A stinging sleet lashed the faces of passers-by.
note: Uncountable; from 'neve'. Verb: nevischiare. Cf. 'nevicata' (snowfall), 'nevaio' (snowfield).

ex: Nella calura del primo pomeriggio il paese pareva deserto.
exEn: In the early afternoon heat the village seemed deserted.
note: Literary/elevated alternative to 'caldo' and 'afa'; 'la calura estiva'. Cf. 'arsura' (parching heat), 'canicola'.

ex: La notte del solstizio d'estate si accendono ancora i falò di San Giovanni.
exEn: On the night of the summer solstice the bonfires of St John are still lit.
note: 'Solstizio d'estate/d'inverno'; adj. 'solstiziale'. Pair with 'equinozio'.

ex: Con l'equinozio di primavera il giorno e la notte tornano ad avere uguale durata.
exEn: With the spring equinox day and night are once again of equal length.
note: Adj. 'equinoziale' (tempeste equinoziali). Learned Latinism; pair with 'solstizio'.

ex: Nel plenilunio d'agosto la campagna era chiara come di giorno.
exEn: Under the August full moon the countryside was as bright as day.
note: Literary and astronomical; everyday 'luna piena'. Opposite: 'novilunio' (new moon). Leopardi's 'Canto notturno' and Pascoli use 'plenilunio'.

ex: Con lo scirocco Venezia si riempie di un'umidità appiccicosa e l'acqua alta minaccia la piazza.
exEn: With the sirocco Venice fills with sticky humidity and the acqua alta threatens the square.
note: From Arabic shuluq. Brings heat, humidity and Saharan dust; 'un tempo da scirocco'. Adj. 'sciroccoso'.

ex: Il maestrale rende la costa occidentale della Sardegna un paradiso per i surfisti.
exEn: The mistral makes Sardinia's west coast a paradise for surfers.
note: The 'master wind' of the rosa dei venti; dry and strong, blows from the Rhône valley across the Tyrrhenian.

ex: Il libeccio alzava onde alte contro il molo di Livorno.
exEn: The libeccio raised high waves against the Livorno breakwater.
note: Brings storms to the Tyrrhenian coast; Carducci's 'San Martino' has 'urla e biancheggia il mar' under it. Adj. 'libecciata' = a libeccio storm.

ex: Un grecale secco e freddo soffiava dalla Grecia sulle coste pugliesi.
exEn: A dry, cold north-easter was blowing from Greece onto the Apulian coast.
note: So called because it blows from the direction of Greece (from the Ionian viewpoint); one of the eight traditional winds.

ex: Il peschereccio fu sorpreso da un fortunale al largo di Lampedusa.
exEn: The fishing boat was caught by a gale off Lampedusa.
note: From 'fortuna' in the old sense of 'fortuna di mare' (storm). Nautical/literary; stronger than 'burrasca'.

en: rime ice; hoar frost on branches and wires
ex: Dopo la notte di nebbia, i pioppi erano rivestiti di galaverna come di merletto.
exEn: After the foggy night, the poplars were coated in rime like lace.
note: Frozen fog deposit, typical of the Pianura Padana; regional-northern origin (also 'calaverna'). Distinct from 'brina' (frost from dew).

ex: Un refolo improvviso fece volare i fogli dal tavolino del caffè.
exEn: A sudden gust sent the papers flying off the café table.
note: Originally Venetian/northern, now literary Italian; gentler than 'raffica'. Trieste's bora comes in 'refoli'.

ex: Una pioviggine fine e insistente inzuppava i cappotti senza che ce ne accorgessimo.
exEn: A fine, persistent drizzle was soaking our coats without our noticing.
note: Verb: piovigginare. Synonyms: 'pioggerella' (more common), 'acquerugiola' (rare, literary).

ex: Anche a luglio bisogna attraversare un nevaio per raggiungere il rifugio.
exEn: Even in July you have to cross a snowfield to reach the hut.
note: Alpine term; a snowfield that survives the summer but, unlike a 'ghiacciaio', does not flow.

en: serac (ice pinnacle or block on a glacier)
ex: Il crollo di un seracco travolse la cordata sotto il Monte Bianco.
exEn: The collapse of a serac swept away the roped party below Mont Blanc.
note: Mountaineering/glaciology; from Savoyard French sérac. 'Seraccata' = ice fall (zone of seracs).

ex: Il crinale appenninico fa da spartiacque tra Tirreno e Adriatico.
exEn: The Apennine ridge acts as the watershed between the Tyrrhenian and the Adriatic.
note: Invariable compound (spartire + acque). Figurative use very common in journalism: 'un evento spartiacque', 'fare da spartiacque'.

ex: La villa sorge su un poggio da cui si abbraccia tutta la valle.
exEn: The villa stands on a knoll from which the whole valley can be taken in.
note: Literary and Tuscan; ubiquitous in place names (Poggibonsi, Poggio a Caiano). Cf. 'colle', 'collina'.

ex: Il sentiero sbuca su un pianoro erboso dove pascolano le mucche.
exEn: The path comes out onto a grassy plateau where cows graze.
note: Smaller than an 'altopiano'; used in hiking descriptions. Learned synonym: 'acrocoro' (large upland plateau).

ex: I fuggiaschi si inoltrarono nella boscaglia per sfuggire alle pattuglie.
exEn: The fugitives pushed on into the scrub to escape the patrols.
note: Slightly pejorative: dense, untended, low woodland (unlike a 'bosco'). Cf. 'sterpaglia', 'macchia'.

ex: Un mozzicone gettato nella sterpaglia bastò ad appiccare l'incendio.
exEn: A cigarette butt thrown into the dry brush was enough to start the fire.
note: Collective from 'sterpo' (dry twig); often plural, 'le sterpaglie'. Standard in news reports on wildfires.

ex: Il sentiero era ormai invaso da un roveto impenetrabile.
exEn: The path had by now been overrun by an impenetrable bramble thicket.
note: From 'rovo' (bramble). Biblical 'roveto ardente' = the burning bush.

ex: La riforma si è cacciata in un ginepraio di ricorsi e cavilli legali.
exEn: The reform has landed itself in a tangle of appeals and legal quibbles.
note: The literal sense is rare; the figurative one ('cacciarsi/ficcarsi in un ginepraio') is standard in journalism.

en: bend, loop (of a river); handle (of a vase)
ex: Il paese si adagia in un'ansa del fiume, protetto su tre lati dall'acqua.
exEn: The village nestles in a bend of the river, protected on three sides by water.
note: Geographical sense; a cut-off loop becomes a 'lanca' (oxbow lake). Also the handle of an amphora and, in anatomy, 'ansa intestinale'.

ex: Il Fondaco dei Tedeschi ospitava a Venezia i mercanti d'oltralpe con le loro merci.
exEn: The Fondaco dei Tedeschi housed the merchants from beyond the Alps in Venice, together with their goods.
note: From Arabic funduq (inn); a combined warehouse, exchange and hostel for foreign traders. In Naples, an old tenement courtyard.

en: widening of a street; small open space
ex: Il mercatino si tiene in uno slargo tra due vicoli, troppo piccolo per chiamarsi piazza.
exEn: The little market is held in a widening between two alleys, too small to be called a square.
note: From 'slargare'; urban-planning and everyday word for an irregular open space that is not quite a piazza.

ex: L'Arsenale di Venezia sfornava una galea al giorno nei momenti di massima attività.
exEn: The Venice Arsenal turned out a galley a day at the height of its activity.
note: Same Arabic root as 'darsena'. Dante cites 'l'arzanà de' Viniziani' (Inf. XXI). Figurative: 'un arsenale di argomenti'.

ex: Pasolini raccontò le borgate romane del dopoguerra in Ragazzi di vita.
exEn: Pasolini depicted the post-war Roman borgate in The Ragazzi.
note: In Rome, the peripheral settlements built under Fascism and after the war; 'borgataro' = inhabitant (colloquial, sometimes derogatory). Elsewhere a small village.

ex: Un cunicolo segreto collegava il castello alla chiesa fuori le mura.
exEn: A secret tunnel linked the castle to the church outside the walls.
note: From Latin cuniculus (rabbit, hence burrow). Used for mines, catacombs, service tunnels; figurative 'i cunicoli della burocrazia'.

ex: Il Broletto di Como, a fasce di marmo bianco e grigio, sorge accanto al Duomo.
exEn: The Broletto of Como, in bands of white and grey marble, stands next to the cathedral.
note: From 'brolo' (enclosed garden) where assemblies met; typical of Como, Brescia, Monza, Novara. Related: 'arengario'.

ex: Il rosone della cattedrale filtra la luce del tramonto in mille schegge colorate.
exEn: The cathedral's rose window filters the sunset light into a thousand coloured splinters.
note: Augmentative of 'rosa'; hallmark of Romanesque and Gothic façades (Orvieto, Assisi). Also a ceiling rose.

ex: Con un salvacondotto del vescovo il mercante attraversò indenne le terre in guerra.
exEn: With a safe-conduct from the bishop the merchant crossed the war-torn lands unharmed.
note: Historical and figurative ('la fama non è un salvacondotto per l'impunità'). Cf. 'lasciapassare'.

ex: I portolani medievali descrivevano coste, porti e fondali con sorprendente precisione.
exEn: Medieval pilot books described coasts, harbours and seabeds with surprising accuracy.
note: Nautical/historical; still used for official sailing directions ('il Portolano del Mediterraneo').

ex: Prima del GPS, il navigatore faceva il punto con il sestante misurando l'altezza del sole.
exEn: Before GPS, the navigator fixed the ship's position with the sextant by measuring the sun's altitude.
note: From 'sesto' (a sixth of a circle). 'Fare il punto' = to take a fix (also figurative: to take stock).

ex: I battelli per le isole partono dall'imbarcadero accanto al municipio.
exEn: The boats for the islands leave from the landing stage next to the town hall.
note: Especially on the northern lakes (Lago Maggiore, Como); from Spanish embarcadero. Cf. 'pontile', 'molo'.

ex: Le cronache degli anni Trenta parlano dell'aeroscalo di Littoria, oggi Latina.
exEn: The chronicles of the 1930s speak of the airfield of Littoria, today Latina.
note: Dated, Fascist-era word; still appears in formal or historical writing. Modern: 'aeroporto', 'scalo aereo'.

ex: Il pilota tentò un ammaraggio d'emergenza nella laguna e tutti si salvarono.
exEn: The pilot attempted an emergency water landing in the lagoon and everyone was saved.
note: From 'mare', modelled on 'atterraggio'; the third of the set is 'allunaggio' (moon landing). Verb 'ammarare'.

en: rounding of the buoy; (fig.) turning point, halfway mark
ex: A quarant'anni sentì di essere arrivato al giro di boa della vita.
exEn: At forty he felt he had reached the halfway mark of his life.
note: From sailing regattas; figurative use dominant ('il giro di boa della legislatura').

ex: Nel novilunio il cielo senza luna offre le condizioni migliori per osservare le stelle.
exEn: At the new moon the moonless sky offers the best conditions for stargazing.
note: Astronomical/literary; everyday 'luna nuova'. Pair with 'plenilunio'.

en: crag, rocky ledge; steep bank; (dress) flounce
ex: Il paese è arroccato su una balza di tufo a strapiombo sulla valle.
exEn: The village is perched on a tufa crag overhanging the valley.
note: Literary-geographical; 'le Balze' near Volterra are famous eroded cliffs. Unrelated fashion sense: flounce.

ex: L'acrocoro etiopico si innalza oltre i duemila metri sul livello del mare.
exEn: The Ethiopian highlands rise above two thousand metres above sea level.
note: Learned geographical Greekism (akros + choros); used of large regional plateaus, not small ones.

en: oxbow lake, cut-off river bend (Po valley)
ex: Le lanche del Ticino sono oasi di aironi e ninfee.
exEn: The oxbow lakes of the Ticino are havens of herons and water lilies.
note: Regional-northern hydrological term (Lombardy, Piedmont); also 'morta' in Emilia.

ex: Le cateratte del Nilo interruppero per secoli la navigazione verso sud.
exEn: The cataracts of the Nile interrupted navigation southwards for centuries.
note: Also spelt 'cataratta'; the same word is the eye condition. Biblical 'si aprirono le cateratte del cielo' = it poured.

en: shoal, sandbank; low water; (fig.) dead end
ex: La barca si è arenata su una secca a poche decine di metri dalla riva.
exEn: The boat ran aground on a sandbank a few dozen metres from the shore.
note: Nautical; 'in secca' = aground, and of rivers 'periodo di secca' (low water). Figurative 'finire in secca' = to grind to a halt.

ex: Il Colosseo e il colonnato di San Pietro sono di travertino cavato a Tivoli.
exEn: The Colosseum and the colonnade of St Peter's are made of travertine quarried at Tivoli.
note: From Latin lapis tiburtinus (stone of Tibur/Tivoli); the building stone of Rome.

ex: Le spiagge di Lipari sono bianche di pomice, che galleggia sull'acqua.
exEn: The beaches of Lipari are white with pumice, which floats on the water.
note: 'Pietra pomice' for scrubbing feet; 'pomiciare' (colloquial: to make out) is unrelated in sense.

ex: I cubetti di porfido trentino pavimentano le piazze di mezza Italia.
exEn: Cubes of Trentino porphyry pave the squares of half of Italy.
note: Hard igneous stone, purple-red or grey; imperial stone of Rome and Byzantium. Adj. 'porfirico'.

ex: Gli uomini del Paleolitico scheggiavano la selce per ricavarne lame e punte.
exEn: Palaeolithic humans knapped flint to make blades and points.
note: Feminine; 'selciato' (cobbled paving) derives from it. Archaeological register.

ex: Il torrente scompare in un inghiottitoio e riemerge chilometri più a valle.
exEn: The stream vanishes into a swallow hole and re-emerges kilometres further down the valley.
note: From 'inghiottire' (to swallow); speleological term. Cf. 'dolina', 'voragine'.

ex: Una pioggia di lapilli e cenere seppellì Pompei in poche ore.
exEn: A rain of lapilli and ash buried Pompeii in a few hours.
note: Volcanological; usually plural. Latin diminutive of lapis (stone).

en: the vault of heaven; the sky
ex: Sotto la volta celeste stellata, il deserto sembrava non avere confini.
exEn: Beneath the starry vault of heaven, the desert seemed to have no limits.
note: Literary fixed phrase; also 'volta del cielo', 'firmamento'. In astronomy 'sfera celeste'.

ex: Il castello domina la valle da uno sperone roccioso inaccessibile.
exEn: The castle dominates the valley from an inaccessible rocky spur.
note: Geographical sense 'sperone di roccia'; also architectural buttress and the rider's spur ('Sperone d'Italia' = the Gargano).

ex: Affrontammo l'ultima erta prima del rifugio con il fiato corto.
exEn: We tackled the last steep climb before the hut, short of breath.
note: Literary; 'stare all'erta' (to be on the alert) comes from sentries standing on a rise. Adj. 'erto' = steep.

ex: L'ostro portava dal mare un'aria tiepida e carica di pioggia.
exEn: The south wind brought warm, rain-laden air from the sea.
note: From Latin auster; 'ostro' (also 'austro') is the poetic name for the south wind of the rosa dei venti. Homonym: 'ostro' = purple dye.
